content.title: Welcome to Python Instructions
content.body: Python is a friendly programming language! Computers follow commands line by line from top to bottom.
content.summary: Use print() to display any message to the screen.

content.description: Test your understanding of printing and command execution order.

questions.text: Which command displays words on the computer screen in Python?
questions.hintText: Think of a printer putting words onto paper.
questions.explanationText: In Python, print() sends output to the terminal or screen.

questions.text: Python runs code from top to bottom, one instruction at a time.
questions.hintText: Imagine reading a comic book panel by panel from top to bottom.
questions.explanationText: Programs execute sequentially line-by-line starting at the first line.

questions.text: Arrange these lines so the program greets the player, asks if ready, and finishes.
questions.hintText: First say welcome, then ask the question, then say mission complete.
questions.explanationText: Sequential order means the greeting must come before the ending.

questions.text: Complete the code to print hi: ____('Hi!')
questions.hintText: The keyword is the standard 5-letter Python display function.
questions.explanationText: We write print('Hi!') to call the print function.

content.description: Learn how variables store data and how numbers work in Python.

questions.text: What will be stored in score after running: score = 10 + 5?
questions.explanationText: Python evaluates the right side 10 + 5 = 15, then stores 15 in score.

questions.text: Variable names in Python can start with a number, for example: 1player = 10.
questions.hintText: Variable names must start with a letter or an underscore.
questions.explanationText: Variable names in Python cannot start with a digit. player1 is valid, 1player is not.

questions.text: Arrange the steps to set gems to 5, collect 3 more, and print total gems.
questions.hintText: Create gems first, add 3, then display the total.
questions.explanationText: You must create the variable first before referencing it in calculations or prints.
In Python, assign values directly to variable names without extra keywords.

content.description: Prove you have mastered basic Python instructions, variables, and sequence!

questions.text: What will print(4 * 2) display on screen?
questions.hintText: In Python, the * symbol performs multiplication.

questions.text: In Python, text strings must always be enclosed in quotes like 'hello' or "hello".
questions.hintText: Without quotes, Python thinks words are variables or commands.
questions.explanationText: Quotes tell Python that the content is plain text (a string).

questions.text: Order the instructions to calculate speed and show it.
questions.hintText: First initialize distance, then calculate speed, then print it.
questions.explanationText: Each line relies on the variable defined on the previous line.

questions.text: Which symbol is used to assign a value to a variable? energy ____ 100
questions.hintText: A single equality symbol assigns a value.
questions.explanationText: The single '=' operator stores the value into the variable.
